Saturating limit it is, and you are right that the factored numerator helps. With products at zero, v = E·ΠS·Q/D, so kcat is the ratio of the leading coefficients of Q and D as the substrates grow: a short calculation in the concentrations only, separate from the :OnlyA limits.

Two details to pin down:
- dead-end corners excluded: take the limit on the mechanism without its dead-end branches, so substrate inhibition through a dead-end complex does not drive kcat to 0. This should reproduce today's values almost everywhere; the vertical slice will measure it;
- mechanisms that never saturate (4 hand-written ones already error today with "no kcat components"): a clear error that names the problem and suggests absolute mode (scale_k_to_kcat = nothing).

Regulators keep today's rule: the maximum over regulator corners, each regulator at zero or saturating.
